sections.heading: BITCOIN MINERS
sections.text: Miners decide on the order of transactions and confirm them by using the Proof of Work consensus algorithm to "mine" for new blocks for the blockchain. In essence, mining secures the Bitcoin network. This process uses lots of energy (mostly sustainable energy and energy that would otherwise be wasted — flare gas, stranded hydro-electric, etc.) in the form of electricity. Miners run the SHA-256 hashing algorithm — a one-way function that takes any input and produces a fixed 64-character output. They repeatedly hash block data + a random number (nonce) through SHA-256, checking if the result starts with enough zeros. It's not 'solving complex math' — it's a brute-force guessing lottery done at incredible speed. What is replace by fee (RBF)? RBF basically works like this - A transaction is created with the RBF flag, indicating that this transaction can be fee bumped - When a fee increase is required, a new transaction is signed, spending one or more of the inputs of the previous transaction, which will remove the old transaction and replace it with this one if some conditions are met - All inputs were not spent or the transactions that spends those UTXOs are in the mempool and have RBF enabled - The TX pays more fees in sats than all the transactions it is replacing - The feerate of the transaction is at least `1 sat/vB` higher than the replaced transactions You may "undo" a payment with this if it's still in the mempool. This is why you shouldn't accept 0/unconfirmed transactions: They are not confirmed and can be "reverted" (replaced by another TX that transfers to the sender's own wallet) ↔RB

There are many clients that have been built, and the user can choose to use whichever client(s) fit his/her needs. Your "profile" (in which you log in with a string of characters called your nsec - like a password) is integrated into whichever client you use or move to (although there will be slight variations of how things are displayed from client to client. Some features may be missing, etc.). Your public profile can be identified from your npub, and can be made even more identifiable by use of a NIP-05 identifier. More on all of these weird words below. A really cool thing about nostr is that Bitcoin Lightning is fully integrated. SATOSHI NAKAMOTO Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonymous creator(s) of Bitcoin. His/their final public correspondence was a post on the bitcointalk.org forum on 12/12/2010: https://bitcointalk.org/index.php?topic=2228.msg29479#msg29479 Satoshi’s final known private correspondence was from an April 26, 2011 email to Gavin Andresen. He wrote: "I wish you wouldn't keep talking about me as a mysterious shadowy figure, the press just turns that into a pirate currency angle. Maybe instead make it about the open source project and give more credit to your dev contributors; it helps motivate them." Theories as to why Satoshi disappeared: https://news.bitcoin.com/satoshis-final-messages-leave-tantalizing-clues-to-his-disappearance/ What we do know is that if Satoshi did reveal himself, he would have to sign the Genesis Block and create a verifiable PGP message to prove his/her identity. - Persons pr
